scope: Lotus Temple (Bahai House of Worship), Delhi
title: Lotus Temple
blurb: The Bahai House of Worship in Delhi, completed 1986 to Fariborz Sahba’s design: 27 white marble petals in three ranks of nine form a lotus 70 m across, sheltering a central prayer hall open to all.

systems.name: Podium
systems.description: The circular podium elevating the temple above the plain, with entrance steps and the plinth ring the petals spring from.

systems.name: Inner petal rank
systems.description: The nine inner marble petals, curving inward to embrace the inner dome.

systems.name: Middle petal rank
systems.description: The nine middle marble petals, curving inward over the inner rank.

systems.name: Outer petal rank
systems.description: The nine outer marble petals, curving outward to form canopies over the nine entrances.

systems.name: Inner dome
systems.description: The double-layered inner dome: 54 concrete ribs with shells between, modelled on the innermost lotus bud.

systems.name: Entrances
systems.description: The nine entrances between the outer petals, each with its door opening onto the central hall.

systems.name: Reflecting ponds
systems.description: The nine reflecting ponds ringing the temple; the lotus grows in water.

systems.name: Walkways and skylight
systems.description: Garden walkways and the central skylight crowning the dome.
